$comment: Worked examples that BOTH rule engines must reproduce exactly.
web/src/engine/evaluate.ts runs the preview build. api/engine.py is the
authority in production. They are separate implementations of one algorithm,
which is a real risk: two engines that disagree would price the same quote two
ways, and the disagreement would show up as a customer receiving a number the
So neither is allowed to change alone. web/src/engine/evaluate.test.ts and
api/tests/test_engine.py both read this file and assert against it. If someone
changes one engine, a test fails on the other side.
The fixtures are deliberately small and made up for this file. Real part
numbers are not used here, because a golden test should say what it is testing
Money is compared to the cent, discounts to four decimal places.
suggestCases exercise `suggest` rather than `evaluate`: candidate filtering, ranking, and the machine-identity grouping that turns 947 Corvus SKUs back into the nine machines they configure.
narrowingCases cover what the application rules out BEFORE anything is
graded — see data/narrowing-rules.json, which they run against directly
rather than through a copy, because the rules are the thing under test.
They use fixtures.narrowingItems rather than fixtures.items so that adding a
printer to make a point does not break the cases that count the others.

cases.name: prices a single line and states margin
cases.why: The base path. 10,000 list at 18% is 8,200 net; cost 5,000 gives 39.02% margin.

cases.name: the tightest cap wins when two rules cap the same part
cases.why: Quoting the looser of two caps is never the safe reading, so 2% beats 5%.

cases.name: a requires rule asks for what is missing, and stops once it is there
cases.why: The rep needs the shortfall, not a restatement of the rule.

cases.name: a lapsed rule does not fire
cases.why: Effective dating is checked before any rule is considered.

cases.name: a rule from another technology does not appear
cases.why: A PALM rule on a CIJ quote teaches a rep to stop reading the trace.

cases.name: an exclude action naming no part never blocks
cases.why: A malformed row must not take every quote down with it.

cases.name: an order-value trigger fires only above its threshold
cases.why: Before the 'total' trigger existed this rule fired on every quote.

cases.name: exceeding a stated maximum raises an approval, it does not block
cases.why: A rep may quote past the ceiling; the quote then names the figure and the ceiling.

cases.name: a discount on a category no line uses raises nothing
cases.why: An unused slider is not a request.

cases.name: a failed eligibility rule blocks and names which conditions failed
cases.why: "No" without "which" is useless to a rep.

cases.name: the same eligibility rule passes when both conditions hold
cases.why: The white-ink printer satisfies condition 1 and the flag satisfies condition 2.

cases.name: margin is withheld, with a reason, when a line has no standard cost
cases.why: A blank that gets read as zero is worse than saying why the number is missing.

expect.marginNoteContains: 1 of 2 lines carry no standard cost

cases.name: fit grading comes from a rule, and names it
cases.why: There is not one threshold compiled into either engine.

cases.name: an empty quote prices to zero and blocks nothing
cases.why: The builder evaluates before anything is added; it must not throw or block.

cases.name: a model list matches the models it names
cases.why: A datasheet states one ceiling for several models, so a rule has to be able to name them. Without this the Python model trigger was untested.

cases.name: a model list does not catch a model it does not name
cases.why: REPORTED SHAPE. Written as 'includes 89' this caught the 6440 too, which made a rule saying only the 6440 is IP65 apply to the 6440. The list names 6400 and 6410; the 6440 must come through clean.

cases.name: a converted threshold is exclusive at the boundary
cases.why: 8.64 mm is 0.34 inch, the top of the stated range, so it is inside it. An inclusive comparison would rule out the exact figure the datasheet permits.

cases.name: one hundredth past the boundary does fire
cases.why: The other half of the boundary: the rule must still work.

cases.name: a stated throw distance fires the rule that reads it
cases.why: Control for the next case.

cases.name: an unconstrained field silences every rule that reads it
cases.why: 'Any throw distance' has to mean the throw rules go quiet, not that they evaluate against a blank and narrow the list anyway. Same profile as the case above, so only noConstraint differs.

cases.name: pickOne questions two alternatives on one quote
cases.why: Five printhead poles of different lengths are a choice, not a kit. Quoting the bracket and the clamp together used to pass in silence.

cases.name: pickOne stays quiet when only one of the set is quoted
cases.why: Choosing one alternative is the correct outcome, not a finding.

cases.name: an absent role fires the bare-printer note
cases.why: role + compareOp 'ne' engages when nothing quoted has that role, so a printer with no accessory can be questioned. A printer sold with nothing to mount it on used to go out silently.

cases.name: the bare-printer note goes quiet once an accessory is on the quote
cases.why: The inverted role trigger must stop engaging as soon as the gap is filled.

cases.name: a role trigger counts distinct items, not quantity
cases.why: Six of one ink is a year's supply; six different service items is somebody adding the whole list. Two accessories at quantity 9 must NOT trip a three-accessory rule.

cases.name: three distinct accessories trips the heap rule
cases.why: This is the shape of 'all the mounting hardware went on the quote'.

cases.name: includesAny matches one term inside free text
cases.why: A substrate is typed by a person, so the rule has to find 'film' inside 'BOPP film, printed'.

cases.name: includesAny stays silent on a substrate nobody listed
cases.why: The comparator must never condemn a substrate for the words it does not contain. 'PETG clamshell' gets silence, not a verdict.

cases.name: a priced line says what the item is
cases.$why: The configurator reads itemRole and model off the priced line to know which requirements a quote already satisfies. Both engines gained the fields in the same session and neither had a case, so they could have drifted silently — which is the exact failure this file exists to prevent.

cases.name: a rule naming a kind of part carries that kind out of the engine
cases.$why: T-BARE fires on 'a printer is quoted and no accessory is'. The kind it wants is in its own trigger, and the screen turns it into a filtered picker. Reading it off the trigger rather than a table means a rule written later gets a picker for free, and means the remedy can never disagree with the condition.

cases.name: a rule that names exact parts offers no picker
cases.$why: T-REQ knows the part number and the shortfall, so it carries a one-click fix instead of a picker. Offering both would be two remedies for one finding, and the screen would have to pick.

cases.name: an item nothing has graded is not called a good fit
cases.$why: The default used to be 'good', so a machine no rule had examined was drawn the same as one a datasheet endorses. Absence of evidence needs its own grade or it silently becomes evidence of absence.

cases.name: room on the pack does not rule a head out
cases.why: REPORTED. markingWindowMm is the space AVAILABLE, and the print-height rules read it as the height REQUIRED — so a 200 mm clear panel ruled out every head printing less than 200 mm. The roomier the product, the fewer machines would take it. A 6 mm code in a 200 mm window fits any of them.

cases.name: an unconstrained character height silences what is derived from it
cases.why: 'Any character height' has to carry to the mark height too, or the shrug is honoured for the question and ignored for the rules behind it.

cases.name: a mark past one head is a chain, not a refusal
cases.why: REPORTED: 'if the mark is too big the tool says nothing will work when a daisy chain would be the solution.' Eight lines of 8 mm is 64 mm of mark on a 25.4 mm head — three heads — and the grade now says so instead of ruling the technology out.

cases.name: past the whole chain it really is a refusal
cases.why: The other side of the same rule. Sixteen lines of 8 mm is 128 mm, past what four chained heads cover, so no number of heads reaches it and the caveat must not fire.

cases.name: an optional line is priced and left out of the total
cases.why: Asked for by the sales team: a rep wants to put a second head or a year of ink in front of the customer without it landing in the price they read. T-PRINTER-A at 18% is 8,200; the optional T-CLAMP is priced at its own 18% — 2 x 164 = 328 — and none of it reaches the order total. Margin is the committed line only: T-INK carries no standard cost, and before this it would have suppressed the margin figure entirely.

cases.name: a flat amount comes off the order and is stated as a percentage
cases.why: Asked for by the sales team: a negotiation ends at 'call it eight thousand', not at a percentage. 10,000 list less 18% is 8,200; 200 off leaves 8,000, which is 20% of list. The percentage is what every ceiling is written in, so it has to be the figure that is reported.

cases.name: a flat amount larger than the quote does not make it negative
cases.why: A typo, and the only safe reading of one. Clamped at the net rather than rejected, because a rep mid-negotiation should see a zero and fix it, not lose the quote.

cases.name: an optional line is not discounted away by the flat amount either
cases.why: The flat amount is money off the ORDER, and an optional line is not on the order. Both mechanisms have to agree about which lines are the quote or the two of them together produce a number from nowhere.

cases.name: a required part's note reaches the rep, and the fix carries the part
cases.why: REPORTED: an item whose description required another item gave no warning, and the part it named could not be found in the catalogue because it is filed under a different technology. The require action answers both — it hands over the part rather than asking the rep to search for it, and the message says why searching would fail. Both engines have to word it the same, because the rep reads one and the service stores the other.

traceHeadlineContains.T-REQ-MSG: filed under VIJ, so the item search will not show it

cases.name: and goes quiet once that part is on the quote
cases.why: The other half. A requirement that keeps asking after it has been met is a warning a rep learns to scroll past.

cases.name: a second solution is graded by its own book, and only by its own
cases.why: A quote carried one technologyCode and rules were chosen by it, so an applicator added to a CIJ quote was priced, totalled, printed on the customer's copy and never graded — silence that reads as approval. Both halves are here: the PALM machine now answers to the PALM rule, and the CIJ printer beside it does not. That second half is the reason the filter existed, and it is enforced per item now rather than per quote.

cases.name: a station answers a question differently from the line
cases.why: A quote holds one application, which is honest for what is true of the line and the room and wrong for what is true of a position on it — the date code on the bottle is not the height of the text on the case label. Measured against the shipped rules, 18 of the 21 book pairs share at least one station-level field, so one answer was serving two stations with nothing saying so. T-FIT-BAD refuses black on dark; the quote says dark corrugated and the CIJ station says white film, so the refusal lifts for it.

cases.name: and a station that says nothing still takes the line's answer
cases.why: Absent means 'same as the line', which is the common case and has to cost nothing to say. The PALM station carries an override for a different field and still inherits the substrate.

cases.name: rounds half up, on the decimal value, in both engines
cases.why: The two engines rounded differently and nothing here could see it. engine.py used round(Decimal(str(n)), N) — half to EVEN — while evaluate.ts used Math.round(n * 100) / 100 — half up on the binary float. Every fixture price in this file was a round hundred, so no case ever produced a half and the corpus asserted agreement it was not testing. These two lines produce one half at each scale, with ordinary money and an ordinary discount. T-ROUND-CENT: 5.00 less 17.5% is 4.125 exactly, so extendedNet is 4.13 and half-to-even would say 4.12. T-ROUND-MILL: 1.05 less 17.5% is 0.86625 exactly, so netUnit is 0.8663 and half-to-even would say 0.8662. Both are the commercial answer: half a cent goes up. Consumables carries no ceiling, so nothing here needs approval and the case is only about arithmetic.

cases.name: two solutions share a price book and are graded apart
cases.why: A solution used to BE a price book — solutions were keyed by technology code, so a quote could hold at most one CIJ station and the second had nowhere to live. A rep quoting two production lines that both need a coder is the ordinary case. Here the same printer is quoted at two stations: the quote says dark corrugated and T-FIT-BAD refuses black on dark, so station one is not recommended; station two answers white film for itself and the refusal lifts. One item number, two solutions, two grades — which is why fit is assessed per (solution, item) and not per item.

cases.name: a station's own 'no constraint' silences rules for that station only
cases.why: The 'any / does not matter' answers are part of the application, so a station that answers the application answers these too. They are NOT merged field by field the way the profile is: a list is answered as a whole, so absent means 'as the quote says' and present — even empty — means this station was asked. Here the quote says dark corrugated and T-FIT-BAD refuses black on dark. Station two waves the substrate off, so the rule goes quiet for it and stays firing for station one. Ticking 'any' on the case labeller must not silence the bottle coder.

suggestCases.name: without an identity, every configuration is its own row
suggestCases.why: The behaviour before grouping, kept as a case so the default cannot change by accident: six CIJ printers in the fixtures, six rows.

suggestCases.name: groups configurations of one machine onto one row
suggestCases.why: Printer Type says which machine a Corvus SKU is; ink and colour say how it is filled. Two machines, four SKUs, two rows, and each says how many ways there are to order it.

suggestCases.name: the representative is the best-graded configuration, not the first
suggestCases.why: Grouping happens after the ranking, so the row that speaks for a machine is the one that fits best. Item numbers alone would have picked 6400-BLACK and 6440-BLACK either way; what this pins is that the identity travels with whichever row wins.

suggestCases.name: an identity attribute already filtered on is not grouped on
suggestCases.why: Once a rep has said which machine, its configurations are exactly what they are looking at. The grouping lifts itself rather than hiding the choice behind the row that made it.

narrowingCases.name: a porous application drops non-porous inks and keeps what says nothing
narrowingCases.why: The base case. The bracket carries neither fact and survives; the non-porous ink states it in words and does not.

narrowingCases.name: a non-porous application is the mirror image
narrowingCases.why: The lookbehind is the whole point: (?<!non-)(?<!non)\bporous\b must drop 'Porous Black' and keep 'Non-Porous (MEK) Black'.

narrowingCases.name: an ink colour is matched by word, not by substring
narrowingCases.why: 'black ink' means Black and Black Thermo and does not mean Blue. The bracket is called 'blue handle' and is an accessory, so the colour words are not read in its description.

narrowingCases.name: grey and gray are one colour spelt two ways
narrowingCases.why: Asking for one must never deny the other, or half a colour's stock disappears on a spelling.

narrowingCases.name: both rules apply together
narrowingCases.why: Porosity and colour narrow independently and compose; only the ink that is both porous and black survives.

narrowingCases.name: an application that says neither narrows nothing
narrowingCases.why: A rule that engages on an empty profile would quietly remove most of a book from a rep who has not told the tool anything yet.

narrowingCases.name: roles decide what is offered at all
narrowingCases.why: suggest() was machine-only with the filter written inline, so the tool went silent about the ink and the bracket the moment a machine was chosen. Machines when the caller says nothing.
